comparison: Perfect agreement on C64-C66 regarding ALSA metric providing robust estimates of local excitability. Both evaluations find these claims supported, with peer reviewers implicitly accepting this as part of 'convincing' turtle cortex results.

Perfect agreement on C67 regarding higher-frequency waves. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of statistical analysis with spiking patterns, while peer reviewers implicitly support this as part of supplementary figures they found 'useful and convincing.' Represents minor disagreement in confidence level.

Perfect agreement on C92-C95 regarding limitations of PLM/PLDC methods. Both evaluations strongly support this critique, with peer reviewers explicitly noting the work shows sequential activation 'can show up as a travelling wave - even in improved methods such as phase delay maps.'

Perfect agreement on C119-C121 regarding justification for turtle preparation. Both evaluations support these methodological claims, with peer reviewers finding methods 'detailed and clearly structured' without challenging the model choice.

Strong agreement on C4, C46-C49 regarding EEG simulation results. Both evaluations support these claims. Peer R1 also includes C74 and C78 which OpenEval addresses separately (R22, R12), showing peer reviewers grouped simulation findings more broadly.

Both address C74 regarding EEG simulation showing discrete activation appearing as continuous waves. OpenEval treats this as separate finding, while peer reviewers group it with broader simulation results (R1). Both find it supported.

Strong agreement on C50-C57 regarding experimental characterization of response timing and propagation. Both evaluations support these claims. Peer R2 additionally includes main conclusions (C6, C7, C59-C63, C73) that OpenEval addresses separately (R7, R9), showing peer reviewers grouped experimental findings more comprehensively.

Both address main experimental conclusions C6, C7, C73 that LFP waves reflect modular activation. OpenEval supports with caveats about DIP test validity and alternative explanations. Peer reviewers provide strong support, calling results 'convincing.' Minor difference in confidence level.

Both address C58-C63 regarding DIP test analysis showing multimodality. OpenEval supports but notes assumptions about distributional properties. Peer reviewers group these with broader experimental findings (R2) and provide strong support. OpenEval more cautious about methodological limitations.

Partial overlap on C58 regarding phase-locking analysis. OpenEval addresses C58-C63 together focusing on DIP test methodology. Peer R5 groups C58 with anatomical interpretation (C105-C106), showing different conceptual grouping of related findings.

Strong agreement on C105-C106 regarding anatomical interpretation of D1/D2 areas. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of systematic mapping and speculative explanation. Peer reviewers implicitly support as part of convincing findings. Represents disagreement in confidence level.

Strong agreement on C5, C68-C72, C75 regarding analytical model of sequential activation. Both evaluations support these claims. Peer R3 also includes C76, C96-C99 which OpenEval addresses separately (R12, R16), showing peer reviewers grouped analytical modeling results together.

Both address C96-C99 regarding analytical model predictions about frequency-dependent and bidirectional waves. OpenEval treats separately from basic model (R11), while peer reviewers group all analytical modeling together (R3). Both find claims supported.

Partial overlap on C76 regarding volume conduction effects. OpenEval addresses C76-C82 together as analytical model results. Peer R3 groups C76 with broader analytical modeling claims, showing different conceptual organization.

Strong agreement on C77-C82 regarding volume conduction and signal spread mechanisms. Both evaluations support these claims. Peer R6 groups these with VSD limitations and filtering effects (C83-C91) that OpenEval addresses separately (R13, R14), showing peer reviewers grouped mechanistic explanations broadly.

Strong agreement on C83-C87 regarding VSD limitations and averaging effects. Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes direct experimental manipulation would strengthen conclusions. Peer reviewers group with broader mechanistic explanations without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on C89-C91 regarding filtering effects promoting wave-like appearance. Both evaluations support these claims. Peer reviewers group with volume conduction and VSD limitations as part of comprehensive mechanistic explanation.

Both address C103-C104 regarding tension between axonal propagation mechanisms and wave diversity. OpenEval supports but notes reliance on inference rather than direct evidence. Peer reviewers group with broader discussion points (R9) and explicitly enjoyed the discussion, providing implicit support.

Both address C100-C102 regarding connection between model and empirical observations. OpenEval supports but notes lack of direct validation in turtle preparation. Peer reviewers group with discussion points and provide positive assessment of 'nice overview of potential options.'

Strong agreement on C107-C114 regarding developmental/pathological waves versus mature cortical function. Both evaluations support these contextual claims. OpenEval notes some inferences are speculative. Peer reviewers explicitly enjoyed the discussion without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on C115-C118 regarding calcium imaging limitations. Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes lack of direct experimental evidence from calcium imaging in the study. Peer reviewers group with broader discussion points and provide positive assessment.

Strong agreement on C1-C2, C8-C18 regarding background on traveling waves. Both evaluations support these introductory claims. Peer R12 groups all background literature (C1-C45) together, while OpenEval separates into traveling waves (R1), modularity (R2), measurement limitations (R3), and prior concerns (R4).

Strong agreement on C19-C26 regarding cortical modularity. Both evaluations support these background claims. Peer reviewers group with all introductory material, while OpenEval treats modularity separately to highlight tension with traveling waves that motivates the study.

Strong agreement on C3, C27-C34 regarding field potential and optical imaging limitations. Both evaluations support these background claims. Peer reviewers group with all introductory material, while OpenEval separates to emphasize methodological context.

Strong agreement on C35-C45 regarding prior concerns about wave measurement validity. Both evaluations support these background claims. Peer reviewers group with all introductory material, while OpenEval separates to highlight knowledge gaps motivating the current study.
